note:
FEATURE / TESTING ARCHITECTURE ISSUE: Revamp repository validation so every production change is tested at both the owning-module level and the assembled-game level, with all visual acceptance performed through the real standalone-player build/capture harness. The normal feature agent should not need to understand or select the harness.

REQUIRED VALIDATION MODEL: For a production change, CI should automatically determine the affected production module(s) from the changed files, run focused automated tests owned by those modules, run each affected player-visible module's local validation scene through the standalone-player build/capture harness, and run `KentridgePlayableSlice` through the standalone-player harness as the canonical top-level game integration/smoke gate.

PLAYMODE IS NOT VISUAL PROOF: PlayMode tests may validate behavior, state, geometry, traversal, contracts, or other runtime semantics, but PlayMode-rendered screenshots are not valid visual acceptance evidence. Any assertion that something visually looks correct must use frames rendered by the built standalone application. Existing PlayMode screenshot tests may remain as diagnostics or behavioral regressions where useful, but they cannot satisfy a visual acceptance gate.

MODULE-OWNED VALIDATION SCENES: Player-visible modules should own small, deterministic validation scenes alongside the module rather than adding feature-validation scenes to the top-level `Assets/Scenes` area. For example, Water should own a scene showing representative still water, shallow shoreline, river flow, waterfall, and terrain-contact cases; structural composition should own representative structural/socket compositions; terrain rendering should own representative terrain cases. These scenes exist specifically to make the owning module easy to inspect and must exercise the real production implementation rather than parallel test-only rendering code.

MODULE SCENE LOCATION: New module validation scenes belong beneath or alongside their owning module/test area rather than the top-level game-scene directory. They do not need to be shipping game scenes or permanently present in normal player build settings. The shared harness must be able to build the requested validation scene directly.

ONE VISUAL HARNESS: There must be one shared standalone-player build/capture mechanism used for module-local visual scenes, `KentridgePlayableSlice`, and SceneIssue visual replay. Do not create module-specific player harnesses. The generic harness must not contain feature-specific knowledge such as mappings from particular test class names to scenes, automatic TownArchitecture/water/castle/Kentridge audit selection, hard-coded feature-specific cameras/walks/screenshot counts/timing based on scene name, or other silent decisions about what proves a feature. Module-owned convention/configuration may describe its validation scene/scenario, but feature agents must not manually invoke or configure harness internals.

AUTOMATIC MODULE DISCOVERY: CI must infer validation from the diff. Production paths map deterministically to owning modules; each module exposes its focused test scope and, when player-visible, its module-local validation scene/scenario through repository convention or module-owned metadata. A normal feature agent changes production code and authors/updates the module's tests and validation scene. CI discovers and executes the required validation automatically. Agents must not manually enumerate test filters, choose scenes, construct harness commands, select screenshot profiles, or know which player-build script implements the gate.

SHARED/CORE CHANGES: When a changed path belongs to shared/core infrastructure or otherwise affects multiple modules, CI must conservatively expand to the known dependent module set or fall back to a broader safe validation set. The burden of determining blast radius must remain in repository/CI dependency rules, not in ad-hoc agent harness selection.

MODULE TESTING RESPONSIBILITY: Focused EditMode/PlayMode tests remain the fast local regression layer and should live with or clearly belong to the changed module. The module-to-test mapping must be deterministic enough for CI to discover automatically from changed paths and repository convention.

KENTRIDGE INTEGRATION GATE: `KentridgePlayableSlice` is the canonical assembled-game integration gate for production changes. It must build and launch as a real player and exercise enough normal gameplay/world generation to detect startup/runtime exceptions, broken world generation, missing or incompatible module integration, traversal/collision failures, rendering/shader failures, and other major regressions visible only when systems are composed. Module validation proves the component itself; Kentridge proves the component still works in the game. Feature agents should not need to explicitly request this gate; CI attaches it automatically to production changes.

SCENE AND SCENARIO: Scene and scenario remain separate concepts internally: the scene identifies where validation runs; the scenario identifies cameras, movement, timing, captures, and assertions. These details should be owned by the module/validation infrastructure and automatically resolved after CI identifies an affected module. The shared runner must not infer scenarios from arbitrary test class names, and normal feature agents should not need to select scenarios manually.

CURRENT ARCHITECTURE TO SIMPLIFY: The current validation path contains special-case mappings between PlayMode test names and scenes, special-case Kentridge evidence behavior, scene-specific visual audits inside the generic player capture path, and agent-authored CI requests that require knowledge of harness details. This issue should replace those mechanisms with automatic diff-based module discovery plus module-owned validation conventions rather than adding another parallel testing path.

AGENT WORKFLOW: Update `AGENTS.md`, SceneIssue workflow instructions, CI semantics, and relevant validation documentation so the normal agent workflow is essentially: modify module production code; add/update focused module tests; for player-visible work add/update the module-local validation scene/content; push. CI determines and runs the module tests, built-player visual validation, and Kentridge integration automatically. Agents must not be expected to choose, invent, extend, or directly understand the standalone-player harness. Remove stale or conflicting workflow references encountered during the migration, including references to non-existent validation documentation.

MIGRATION PROOF: Demonstrate the architecture by migrating at least one representative player-visible module, preferably Water, to a module-local validation scene and proving that a normal production diff automatically triggers the complete flow without manually naming harness targets: focused module tests -> built-player module visual validation -> built-player `KentridgePlayableSlice` integration. The migrated visual scene must use the production module implementation and its visual proof must come only from the standalone-player harness.

ACCEPTANCE:
(1) Production file paths map deterministically to owning module(s), and CI derives the affected validation set automatically from the diff.
(2) Each module has a deterministic convention or module-owned metadata for its focused automated tests and, where applicable, module-local validation scene/scenario.
(3) Player-visible modules can own validation scenes beneath/alongside their module rather than placing all validation scenes in top-level `Assets/Scenes`.
(4) The standalone-player harness can build and capture an automatically discovered module validation scene without requiring test-name-to-scene inference or permanent normal-build registration.
(5) All visual acceptance uses standalone-player output. PlayMode-rendered screenshots or RenderTextures may remain diagnostic but cannot satisfy a visual acceptance gate.
(6) Every production-module change automatically runs focused tests for affected modules plus the canonical built-player `KentridgePlayableSlice` integration gate.
(7) Affected player-visible modules additionally run their module-local visual scene/scenario automatically through the same standalone-player harness.
(8) Normal feature agents do not manually select test filters, scenes, scenarios, screenshot profiles, player-build commands, or CI harness options. The required validation is inferred from changed files and module ownership.
(9) Shared/core changes conservatively expand to dependent modules or a broader safe validation set without requiring the agent to enumerate consumers manually.
(10) Remove or migrate generic-harness special cases that infer feature-specific audits, camera behavior, timing, screenshot requirements, or scenes from arbitrary test names/scene names. Required behavior belongs in reusable infrastructure or module-owned validation configuration.
(11) Scene and scenario are represented separately enough that multiple automatically discovered validation targets can use the same shared runner without embedding feature policy in shell/CI infrastructure.
(12) Update `AGENTS.md`, SceneIssue workflow instructions, CI semantics, and relevant validation docs to describe the simple module-author workflow and hide harness implementation details. Remove stale references such as `SceneIssues/feature-readme.md` if it remains absent.
(13) Preserve exact-SHA CI/evidence requirements and fail when an automatically required focused test, module scene, built-player capture, or Kentridge integration gate does not actually execute. A zero-match test or skipped required target cannot count as green.
(14) Migrate at least one representative visual module, preferably Water, to a module-local validation scene and prove that an ordinary production diff automatically triggers `focused module tests -> built-player module visual validation -> built-player Kentridge integration`.
(15) The migration does not create a second standalone-player harness, module-specific build implementation, or another parallel CI transport.
(16) Existing useful focused regressions remain available, but visual acceptance semantics are removed from PlayMode-only evidence paths.
(17) The resulting architecture is simpler to explain than the current system: agents author module code/tests/scenes; CI discovers what changed; module tests prove the module contract; module-local built-player scenes prove player-visible output; built-player Kentridge proves assembled-game integration.
(18) Measure CI/runtime cost and keep the architecture suitable for routine agent iteration. Avoid unrelated module visual scenes, while every required affected-module and Kentridge gate must execute automatically before final production validation can pass.
